children: Investor sentiment in Germany jumped in November despite the lingering energy shock driven by the war in Iran, with government stimulus and strong exports supporting an improving economic outlook.

The ZEW Indicator of Economic Sentiment for Germany, which tracked the expectations of 194 analysts and investors at banks, insurance companies and other businesses, rose by 7.5 points on month to 35.6. A consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expected the reading to remain unchanged at 28.1.
Investor confidence was last higher in February, before the outbreak of war in between the U.S. and Iran sent energy prices skyrocketing and sentiment into negative territory.
"The German economy remains on its recovery track, albeit moving at a slow rate," said ZEW president Achim Wambach.
Rising manufacturing orders and falling oil prices are likely to continue underpinning economic expectations, while government investment is also driving a recovery, Wambach said.

The European Commission on Tuesday sharply upgraded its forecast for German economic growth this year to 1.3% from 0.6%, reflecting a stronger-than-expected recovery supported by government spending and exports.

"This acceleration is supported mainly by a surge in exports in early 2026, which is set to further benefit in 2027 from the global AI boom, and from an expansion in defense and infrastructure expenditure," the commission said.
The German economy continued to expand by 0.2% in the third quarter, its fourth consecutive quarter of growth.
